newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Yuan bond unacceptable for HK Exchange Fund-report.
newsitem.headline: Yuan bond unacceptable for HK Exchange Fund-report.

text.p: Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) chief executive Joseph Yam was quoted on Thursday as saying Hong Kong's Exchange Fund would not invest in China's yuan-denominated national bonds.

"Unless the renminbi (yuan) can be fully convertible and China's sovereign credit rating improves, it (Chinese bonds) will not be accepted as an investment vehicle of the Exchange Fund," Yam told the Hong Kong Economic Journal in London.
China could not force Hong Kong to invest in yuan bonds so talk of using Hong Kong's reserves to suppport the mainland's budget deficit was groundless, he said.
But because China's economic development was rapid, if one day the yuan became fully convertible and China's credit rating improved, Hong Kong would consider investing in yuan bonds, Yam added.
Hong Kong's Exchange Fund with assets of HK$461 billion at end-1995 was established to back the Hong Kong dollar, which is pegged with the U.S. dollar at HK$7.8 to US$1.
The British colony reverts to Chinese sovereignty next year.
